children: A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after the U.S. Commerce Department moved to close a loophole allowing Chinese companies to lease Nvidia computing power from locations in other countries, CNBC reported, compounding hot wholesale inflation data and Nvidia’s leadership turmoil ahead of its earnings call under interim CEO Colette Kress.

Commerce’s action marks the first U.S. policy response to the scandal behind former CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation.UBS trimmed its Nvidia price target to $240 from $300 ahead of the earnings report, citing potential export curbs on markets such as Singapore and Malaysia, CNBC noted.

High-speed switches and custom interconnects ship in lumpy waves tied to data-center GPU deployments. If closing third-country compute loopholes curtails overseas cluster builds and Kress signals export bottlenecks during Nvidia’s earnings call, networking vendors face near-term valuation compression.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.
Among others, the following stocks were impacted:
Enterprise networking company Vistance Networks fell 6.6%.
Enterprise networking company Arista Networks fell 5.4%.
Enterprise networking company Applied Digital fell 8.9%. Is now the time to buy Applied Digital?

children: Applied Digital’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 103 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

Applied Digital is down 48.3% since the beginning of the year, and at $14.53 per share, it is trading 70.7% below its 52-week high of $49.65 from May 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Applied Digital’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $598.04.
